executiveSummary: Q3 FY26 revenue fell 11% to $19.6M as two enterprise customers left and churn doubled. We have cut $6M of run-rate cost, found the cause in onboarding, and ask the board to approve a $4M retention plan that returns us to growth by Q2 FY27.

slides.slideTitle: Q3 FY26: a hard quarter, and the plan to turn it
slides.subtitle: Board update · Calder Health · November 2026
slides.speakerNotes:
- I will not soften this. Q3 was our worst quarter in three years.
- I will show you why, what we have already done, and what we need from you.

keyBullets: What happened in Q3
Why it happened
What we have already done
The plan, and what we ask of you
slides.speakerNotes: - Four parts. Decisions at the end.

slides.subtitle: Quarterly revenue, $M
keyBullets: Our first decline in twelve quarters
slides.speakerNotes:
- $19.6M against $22.0M in Q2.
- $1.9M of the drop is two enterprise accounts.

keyBullets: monthly logo churn in Q3, up from 2.1% in Q4 FY25
slides.speakerNotes:
- This is the number that matters most.
- Every point of churn costs us about $2.6M a year.

slides.slideTitle: Margin and cash are falling with it
keyBullets: 51%: gross margin, down 7 points in a year
$28.7M: cash, down $12.3M since Q4 FY25
14 months: runway at Q3's burn
slides.speakerNotes:
- Margin fell because we kept implementation staff while revenue fell.
- Runway is 14 months if nothing changes. Things will change.

slides.slideTitle: We lost customers in their first 90 days
slides.subtitle: 71% of Q3's churned accounts had not finished onboarding
slides.speakerNotes:
- We pulled every churned account.
- Seven in ten never got through onboarding. It is not the product. It is how we start.
slides.purpose: The turn: the cause is found

keyBullets: Implementation queue grew from 9 to 31 days
One onboarding lead for every 40 new accounts
No health check before go-live
Sales promised integrations we had not built
slides.speakerNotes: - Each of these is fixable, and none needs new product.

keyBullets: Done: cut $6M of run-rate cost
Done: froze hiring outside onboarding
In progress: queue down to 14 days
Next: health check before go-live
slides.speakerNotes: - We did not wait for this meeting. Cost is already out.

keyBullets: Now (Q4): queue under 10 days; onboarding team doubled; health checks live
Next (Q1 FY27): churn under 3%; win back the two lost accounts
Then (Q2 FY27): revenue growing again; margin back to 56%
slides.speakerNotes: - Three steps. Each has a number we will report against.

keyBullets: $2.5M to double the onboarding team
$1.0M for the go-live health check
$0.5M for win-back offers to churned accounts
slides.speakerNotes:
- This is the decision we need today.
- It keeps runway above 12 months.

keyBullets: Hiring: we may not fill 12 onboarding roles by January
Competition: Medora is pricing 20% under us in mid-market
slides.speakerNotes: - If hiring slips, we pull in partners. If pricing bites, we hold price and sell outcomes.

slides.slideTitle: Back to growth by Q2 FY27
slides.subtitle: Churn under 3% · runway above 12 months · revenue growing again
slides.intent: Leave the board with the target
